newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN GENERAL NEWS - AUG 14.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday launched a comprehensive and politically courageous tax reform plan, including consideration of a new consumption tax, substantial income tax cuts and a review of Commonwealth-State financial relations. Howard also anounced a special Premiers Conference and the formation of a high-level task force to develop tax reform options. Page 1.

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia yesterday announced a A$5 billion alliance with outsourcing giant Electronic Data Systems (EDS). The deal will transfer all the bank's information technology operations to EDS Australia with the bank taking a 35 per cent equity stake in the company. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday claimed the Federal Government's micro-economic reforms had increased the possibility of sustained economic growth of over 4.5 per cent. Particular reforms highlighted by Howard for removing obstacles to growth included the Government's fiscal consolidation strategy, industrial relations reforms and its privatisation program. Page 3.

Amcor Ltd's paper manufacturing division, Australian Paper, has secured workforce support for an innovative "gain sharing" deal. The new enterprise agreement will see blue-collar workers at Australian Paper plants eligible for annual lump-sum payments liked to the company's financial performance. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard has taken a political risk and ensured that tax reform will be the pivotal issue at the next election. Central to his promotion yesterday of the Federal Government's tax reform agenda was his support for income tax reductions in return for a goods and services tax. Page 1.

Federal Opposition leader Kim Beazley has attacked the Federal Government's tax reform agenda and vowed to oppose Prime Minister John Howard's push for a goods and services tax. Beazley characterised the Federal Government's announcement of a new tax inqiry as a "secret, bureaucratic investigation", and forecast the Coalition would impose a GST of 20 per cent or more. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard has added his voice to that of Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane in promoting the economy's growth prospects. Howard welcomed Macfarlane's support for strong growth policies now that inflationary pressures were under control but stopped short of endorsing the 4.5 per cent annual growth target proposed by the RBA governor. Page 2.

Imitating the tactics employed by Rio Tinto at its Hunter Valley No. 1 mine, American-owned Queensland coal company ARCO Coal yesterday confirmed it had ordered mine operators Curragh Queensland Coal Mining to resume production at the open cut mine using non-union labour. The move follows a 14-week strike at the mine by union workers who oppose the company's plans to radically reform work practices. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Federal Government has undertaken to proceed to the next election with a comprehensive taxation reform package aimed at reducing personal income tax. Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday part of this reform must be a consideration of the introduction of a broad-based indirect tax, and again vowed to keep his election promise and not introduce any new taxes before the next election. Page 1.

The New South Wales Liberal party is apprehensive of a return to open conflict between its Right and Left factions after recent allegations of branch stacking. The division among the party was highlighted by the attendance of Lyenko Urbanchich, a central figure in the factional struggles of the 1980s, at a meeting of senior party members opposed to the growing influence of the faction known as The Group. Page 1.

Deputy New South Wales Premier Andrew Refshauge yesterday risked his leadership of the Left faction by supporting the sale of a group of State assets as an alternative to the proposed sale of the NSW electricity industry. Refshauge's comments also placed him in opposition to Premier Bob Carr and Treasurer Michael Egan who advocate the electricity sale. Page 1.

Expatriate Australian fiction writer Shirley Hazzard last night delivered the Sydney Institute's 1997 Larry Adler Lecture, titled Bread and Circuses: Thought and Language in Decline. Hazzard gave her support for an Australian republic but warned of the dangers of technological change. Page 1.
THE AGE

In an attempt to counter falling community support and perceptions the Federal Government is in mid-term doldrums Prime Minister John Howard signalled yesterday he would promote tax reform as the central issue at the next election, expected late in 1998. The tax reform agenda announced yesterday proposes radical reforms of Australia's tax and finance system. Page 1.

The Federal Government has authorised an investigation into allegations the Khmer Rouge commander who ordered the execution of Australian backpacker David Wilson is under the personal protection of Hun Sen. Former Cambodian finance minister Sam Rainsy said yesterday the commander Noun Paet was among the Khmer Rouge defectors allied to Hun Sen. Page 1.

Car manufacturer Toyota announced yesterday prominent businessman James Packer would join car dealer Nick Polites and become an equity partner in the Toyota dealership, Melbourne City Toyota. The move is part of Toyota's attempt to boost its Victorian sales by establishing giant car supermarkets. Page 1.

The generation born in the mid-to-late 1950s is preparing to assume the political leadership of Australia from the baby boomers and older generations. Among this group are Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and Health Minister Michael Wooldridge and Labor' transport spokesman Lindsay Tanner and education spokesman Mark Latham. Page 1.
